sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Ruby uses modules in place of multiple inheritance, and understanding exactly how include, extend, and prepend each affect the method lookup chain is a mandatory interview topic at any serious Rails shop. Include inserts the module above the class in the ancestors chain; extend adds the module's methods as singleton methods; prepend inserts the module before the class, enabling method wrapping without monkey-patching. This page covers all three, plus the two most powerful standard mixins: Enumerable (implement each, get the entire collection API for free) and Comparable (implement <=>, get all comparison operators). Every answer explains the MRO impact so you can reason about method dispatch, not just recite the difference.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: include-extend-prepend, comparable-enumerable, module-patterns, scenario-based. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
